rationale:
Closing the one substantive objection the council raised against migration 602 (bug_historian, advisory medium, corr c962abd1, APPROVED round 1). Quoting it: the picker steps route error_step TO the saving step with no durable record, so "a repeated LLM-picker failure would be invisible except by absence-of-effect".

The fail-open routing is right and is not changing: a cross-mention must never fail a tool build. What was wrong is that the emitter then recorded `no_related_pages` with an EMPTY `related_pages_source` — which is byte-identical to what a picker that ran and correctly answered "none" produces. So a picker failing on every single build was indistinguishable from a site with no topically-matching pages, and the emitter recorded the reassuring one of the two.

That is bugs_open/330's own root cause for the third time. 330 §2's confirmed defect was that ExtractActionInputs' strategy0Resolved bookkeeping stored "I tried and found nothing" and "I was never asked" identically; §12 found the same shape in the emitter's skip prose ('a suggestion may legitimately name no related pages', written for items no suggester ever saw); this is the third instance, one layer along, in the field the 602 picker writes.

The fix is available because a `?` OPTIONAL-EXPLICIT key is written ONLY by the explicit-path arm (RFC_029 D2): if the picker step errored to error_step its output field does not exist and the key is ABSENT; if it ran it is PRESENT and holds the answer, empty or not. `ActionInputs.Has` (action_inputs.go:554, `ok && v != nil`) is exactly that distinction and already exists.

It also splits out a THIRD state nobody had noticed, and it is the one worth chasing: a picker that ran and returned something that is not a page list at all — prose, a refusal sentence, a malformed answer. That is a prompt or model fault, it was silent, and it is NOT the same event as an honest refusal. Two states would have hidden it behind the third.

plan.summary: One function and its constants: the empty-source case becomes three named outcomes — no_picker (never ran / failed to error_step), picker_declined (ran, none fit — a correct answer per the prompt's rule 5), picker_unusable (ran, answer unreadable). No behavioural change to which pages are chosen, no change to precedence, no change to the fail-open routing. Sketches are pasted WHOLE from the file, not excerpted — the previous round's three objections were all about what a 900-character truncation hid (WRONG_CALLS 2026-08-25).

edits.rationale: The three-way split, at the only point that can see it. The requester-wins precedence above is untouched — this arm is reached only when nothing supplied pages, and its whole job is to say WHICH kind of nothing. `Has` is the load-bearing call: a marked key is written only by the explicit-path arm, so absent means the step produced no output field, which means it never ran or it errored to error_step.

Classifier separating a well-formed empty answer from an unreadable one. Arms mirror relatedPagesFromSpec deliberately: a list type IS a list, and reaching here means it was empty or all-blank, so the picker declined; a string counts only if it parses as the JSON array the prompt demands. Anything else is a model that stopped obeying the output format, which needs chasing rather than filing as an honest 'none'.

Five named constants rather than three plus an empty string, because these values are written into durable rows (agent_error_log context and every emitted item's spec) and read back by census queries — a typo or a collapsed pair is invisible until someone counts. Each carries what it MEANS, not just what it is.

Four new cases on the existing harness, which already drives the real extractor with the live optional-explicit config: never-ran, ran-and-declined (string `[]`), ran-and-returned-prose, and ran-and-returned-an-empty-array-VALUE (the same answer arriving as a Go slice rather than a string — both spellings must classify identically, since which one you get depends on how the step's output was stored). The mismatch message now prints the case's own reasoning, so a future failure explains itself.
edits.sketch:
cases: {no picker in collected} -> no_picker · {result: `[]`} -> picker_declined · {result: "Sorry, none of these pages fit."} -> picker_unusable · {result: []interface{}{}} -> picker_declined
assert: source == tc.wantSource, message carries tc.why

grounded_in: The objection being closed, verbatim from the round-1 council_report for corr c962abd1 (bug_historian, severity medium): "Migration 602 routes the new picker steps' error_step directly to 'save_tool' (the happy-path continuation) with no visible logging/error-record step in between... a repeated LLM-picker failure would be invisible except by absence-of-effect."
The mechanism is not invented: datahelpers.ActionInputs.Has, action_inputs.go:554, returns `ok && v != nil` — present-and-non-nil. Read first-hand before designing on it.

A `?` marked field never meets ExtractFields and is written only by the explicit-path arm (action_inputs.go, the withoutStrict/explicitOnly block, RFC_029 D2) — which is what makes absence mean 'the step produced no output', rather than 'the search did not find one'.

The picker is LIVE and has produced a real result: llm_call_log agent_type='tool-generator' step_name='suggest_related_pages' at 2026-08-25 09:50:53Z, success, reply ["learn-accessibility-focus-states","learn-design-oklch-colors"], and two site_work_items at 09:50:59Z stamped related_pages_source='suggested'. So this is a change to a mechanism with observed traffic, not a speculative one.

Mutation-proved in a git-archive-HEAD copy (verify-head-builds.sh --with, KEEP_TREE=1, mutated inside the kept tree so the shared working copy never held a mutation): dropping the Has() check fails the never-ran case; making the classifier always-true fails the prose case; dropping its []interface{} arm fails the empty-array case. Each failure names the case it was written for, and the other cases keep passing.
Full package green against committed HEAD e062df96f with the change overlaid, and go build ./platform/... clean.
plan.risks:
1. The empty-source value disappears from new rows. Nothing queries related_pages_source yet — it shipped 2026-08-24 and its only consumers are the RUNBOOK's verification queries, which I own and am updating in the same change. Existing rows keep their empty string; a census spanning the change must treat '' and 'no_picker' as the same bucket, and that is stated in the runbook rather than left to be discovered.

2. picker_unusable could fire on a shape that is actually fine — e.g. a future step storing its output as a map. Bounded: it is a label on a path that already produced no pages, so no behaviour changes either way; the cost of a mislabel is a wasted look, not a wrong link.

3. This does not add a durable record on the LOAD step's failure, which runs before any model call. That failure still leaves no llm_call_log row and now reports no_picker — which is CORRECT and is the point, but it does not distinguish 'load failed' from 'step unwired'. Stated rather than fixed; the runbook names the signature (skips with no picker calls at all).

4. Inert until a chassis roll, like any Go change here. The council-approved 602 config is already live, so between this commit and the roll the empty-source ambiguity persists exactly as today — no window is opened that was not already open.
